title: ammoniaRateBench operation
description: The ammonia synthesis rate of Dyson & Simon (1968) — Ind. Eng. Chem. Fundam. 7(4) 605-610 — as a cited correlation object, in three parts. VERIFY (always): five anchors, each stating whether it is THEORY (an identity the expression must satisfy, such as Eq 19's two terms having ratio (Ka/Q)^2) or ARITHMETIC (the closed form at a stated point against a literal, which proves a TRANSCRIPTION and never a physics). Nothing here is measured by Choupo: the data these equations were fitted to are Nielsen, Kjaer and Hansen's. LOCUS (optional): sweeping temperature at a fixed nitrogen conversion on the paper's own reference mixture locates the temperature of greatest net rate, and three conversions show that locus DESCENDING — the curve a quench converter zigzags about. POINTS (optional): the rate at states the case declares. Note the SYMBOL COLLISION: the paper writes xi for the effectiveness factor and eta for the conversion of nitrogen, which is the opposite of CatalystPellet.H and of most textbooks.

catalyst.title: The catalyst particle
catalyst.description: There is NO default particle size: which branch of Eq 39/40 applies depends entirely on it, so omitting this block makes Equation 40 refuse by name rather than assume one.

particleDiameter.title: Particle diameter
particleDiameter.description: Below 6 mm the effectiveness factor is exactly 1 and that is the AUTHORS' position, not an assumption of ours. Between 6 and 10 mm it comes from Eq 39 with Table I. Above 10 mm the correlation refuses: a larger particle is a different diffusion problem, not a further value of this one.

locus.title: The locus of maximum rate
locus.description: Optional. Sweep temperature at each declared conversion and report where the net rate is greatest.

pressure.title: Pressure
pressure.description: The correlation's window is 150 to 300 atm. Equation 39 is TABULATED at exactly 150, 225 and 300 atm and has no form in pressure, so it is linearly interpolated between them (announced — Choupo's choice, not the paper's) and REFUSED outside them. The rate expression itself only announces out there, because it is a closed expression and Eq 39 is a table.

conversions.title: Nitrogen conversions (the paper's eta)
conversions.description: Conversion of nitrogen measured from the reference mixture — 3:1 H2/N2 with 12.7 % inerts — at which eta = 0. One conversion gives one point of the locus; the locus is the sequence, and a single point cannot show that it descends.

temperature.title: Temperature sweep
temperature.description: The window swept at each conversion. A maximum found ON an end of it is reported as an edge rather than as a maximum.

to.title: Upper temperature
to.description: End of the sweep; must exceed `from`.

n.title: Points
n.description: Number of temperatures swept, at least 2.

points.title: Declared states
points.description: Optional. Evaluate the rate at gases the case declares — typically the bed states another case computed. Nothing is ranked or compared.

label.title: Name
label.description: A single word; it keys this state's published diagnostics.

P.title: Pressure
P.description: Gas pressure. Converted to atmospheres inside, which is the unit Eqs 6-8 were written in.

composition.title: Bulk mole fractions
composition.description: Must sum to 1: a composition that does not close is REFUSED rather than normalised, because renormalising would hide which of the four is wrong. Equation 19 divides by X_NH3, so a gas with no ammonia has no finite rate and refuses too.

inert.title: Inerts
inert.description: Mole fraction of the inerts, lumped — the paper's species 4.
